panels.rationale: Single clinical photograph of a neonate (1 hour of life) from a case report titled 'Transient neonatal pustular melanosis: An unusual and challenging eruption', so the eruption is attributed to the configured target disease. However, the morphology shown is unusual (desquamation with flaccid/ruptured/purulent vesicles and bullae) and the text explicitly notes the absence of small simple pustules, so only truncal pustule/purulent lesions could be mapped to the vocabulary and confidence is moderate; the article itself labels the eruption unusual and challenging.
panels.attribution_text: Boffa et al. Transient neonatal pustular melanosis: An unusual and challenging eruption.. Clinical case reports 2023. doi:10.1002/ccr3.8092. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Image taken at 1 hour of life depicting areas of desquamation with a mixture of vesicles and bullae that were either flaccid, ruptured or purulent, over the trunk, face, head, and neck.
in_text_mentions: ted to have a rash that consisted of generalized desquamation over the face, head, neck, trunk, and limbs (including the digits but excluding the palms and soles) with vesicles and bullae, ranging from 3 to 8 mm in diameter, some flaccid and some containing white fluid. There was also evidence of ruptured bullae with residual erythematous, raw skin, but no small, simple pustules (Figures 1 and 2). Of note were patches of desquamation over the back, with a large patch over the buttocks, and some annular desquamated lesions over the scalp (Figure 3). The mucosae and conjunctivae were unaffected.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Clinical photograph of a neonatal back taken at 1 hour of life showing flaccid bullae and patchy desquamation. The disease-focused article title and caption support attribution to transient neonatal pustular melanosis, but the visible manifestations are atypical and are not represented in the provided finding vocabulary. B: Clinical photograph of a neonatal scalp taken at 1 hour of life showing annular desquamation and erythema. The disease-focused article title and caption support attribution to transient neonatal pustular melanosis, but the visible manifestations are atypical and are not represented in the provided finding vocabulary.

panels.rationale: Real clinical photograph of a neonate a few days after birth showing sparse vesicles/bullae and erythematous residual patches on the back, in an article titled 'Transient neonatal pustular melanosis: An unusual and challenging eruption'. The vesiculobullous rather than pustular morphology is a recognized (captioned as unusual) presentation, so typicality is variant rather than classic; disease attribution rests on the disease-focused article title plus the captioned neonatal eruption.
